title: SLO telemetry sprint sequence and handoff checklist
content:
Context: This is a working-level plan to deliver a repeatable sprint sequence for SLO telemetry onboarding, plus a short handoff checklist for feature teams to go from feature-complete -> production SLO coverage. Purpose is to reduce the end-to-end time to instrument and validate SLOs for new model-serving routes and to create a clear telemetry taxonomy for cross-team handoffs.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-first-SLO from feature complete to < 3 sprints for high-priority routes.
- Standardize signal taxonomy so alerts/dashboards are consistent across services.
- Create a one-page handoff checklist that platform/feature teams can follow.

Scope:
- Primary focus: model-serving API endpoints, async batch-runs, and caching layer.
- Out of scope: infra-only changes to GPU schedulers and billing metrics (separate project).

Sprint sequence (recommended 3 x 2-week sprints):
Sprint 0 (pre-sprint, ~1 week) - prep:
- Inventory endpoints and owner contacts (TODO: owners list, see JIRA SRE-3421).
- Run sampling of traces and token-latency distributions for baseline.
- Create baseline dashboard template (copy of obs/dashboard-template-v2).

Sprint 1 - Instrument + surface signals:
- Add instrumentation for the defined signal taxonomy (below) to feature env.
- Ship metrics to observability pipeline, validate cardinality limits.
- Basic dashboard with p50/p95/p99, error rate by class, availability.
- Lightweight smoke alerts (error-rate > 1% over 5m).

Sprint 2 - Validate + simulate errors:
- Run chaos-like traffic patterns (latency spikes, KV-cache misses) to validate signals.
- Introduce synthetic traffic to exercise tail latencies.
- Refine SLA -> SLO conversion and set initial error budget burn policy.

Sprint 3 - Harden + handoff:
- Finalize dashboards and alert thresholds.
- Complete runbook and oncall playbook snippets.
- Handoff checklist completed and signed off by service owner + SRE.

Telemetry signal taxonomy (core signals - required):
- request.latency.microsec (p50,p95,p99)
- request.success.count and request.failure.count (tagged by error_class)
- model.kv_cache.hit_ratio (percent)
- batch.job.duration.seconds and batch.job.failure_rate
- api.throttled.count and quota_exhausted.count
- request.queue.depth and worker.utilization

Derived signals (recommended):
- error_budget_burn_rate (rolling 1h, 24h)
- slow_path_ratio (requests triggering fallback models)
- token_emit_rate and token_cost_per_request

Dashboards & alert rules (notes):
- Use single dashboard per service with a top row of "health" KPIs: availability, p95 latency, error budget burn.
- Alerts must be actionable and include runbook links. Avoid duplicate alerts across infra and app levels.
- Do not create high-cardinality alert labels (e.g., user_id) — enforce cardinality policy via datadog/prometheus relabel.

Handoff checklist (to be completed by feature team before SRE sign-off):
- [ ] Instrumentation code merged and deployed to staging.
- [ ] Dashboard seeded from template and visible to SRE.
- [ ] Synthetic workload and failure tests executed; results attached.
- [ ] Initial SLO definition documented (target, window, measurement method).
- [ ] Error budget policy proposed (auto-throttle, rollout freeze, or notify).
- [ ] Runbook draft created and linked from dashboard.
- [ ] Owner, oncall rotation, and escalation contacts listed.
- [ ] Post-deploy smoke (10k synthetic requests or 24h production sampling) completed.

Roles & RACI (high level):
- Feature Team: Responsible for instrumentation, test traffic, and runbook draft.
- SRE: Accountable for final SLO verification, dashboards, and alert tuning.
- Observability Platform: Consulted for pipeline/ingest limits and dashboard templates.
- Product/PM: Informed of SLO targets for customer-impacting flows.

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: High-cardinality metrics cause ingest cost blowout.
  Mitigation: Enforce tag whitelist; review sample cardinality in sprint 0.
- Risk: Alerts that are non-actionable create noise.
  Mitigation: Start with conservative thresholds; require alert playbook before escalation.
- Risk: SLOs misaligned with product expectations.
  Mitigation: early engagement with PM and include SLO tradeoffs in sprint review.

Operational notes / quick wins:
- Reuse existing observability templates: obs/dashboard-template-v2 and obs/alert-playbook-minimal.
- Use synthetic traces with real seed prompts for LLM endpoints (do not leak PII).
- Prefer counter-based error budgets over naive uptime metrics for model-serving flows.

Open questions / TODOs (working):
- Decide default SLO windows for model endpoints (30d vs 7d) - (action: PM + SRE to propose).
- Confirm quota/limits for token-level metrics in the hosted pipeline (ask observability infra).
- Agree on ownership for fallback-model signals (platform vs feature).

Next steps (short):
1) Assign owners for inventory by 2025-04-04 (owner: Lina).
2) Kickoff sprint-0 prep and get baseline sampling outputs by 2025-04-11.
3) Create draft handoff one-pager and circulate to eng leads (target 2025-04-18).

Notes to self: keep the handoff checklist intentionally minimal — teams often skip long forms. This doc will be the "short path" for teams that want SRE signoff quickly.

References: Confluence: inf-ops/slo-telemetry-cookbook, JIRA: SRE-3421, Slack: #sre-slo-onboarding

End of working draft.
